records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: arXiv preprint, submitted August 2026; no peer-reviewed publication identified by 2026-08-24
records.decision_reason: The paper operationalizes bottom-up LLM open coding, label consolidation, and expert validation on student-tutor dialogue.

Research objective.value: Build and validate a bottom-up taxonomy of the discourse students produce while using a Socratic AI physics tutor.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: Emergent open coding framed as the LLM analogue of grounded-theory open coding.
Claimed qualitative methodology.anchor: This is the LLM analog of open coding

Actual operationalized methodology.value: GPT-5.4-mini assigned a free-text discourse label to each student turn using four preceding conversational turns; text-embedding-3-small and average-linkage agglomerative clustering consolidated labels; an LLM named clusters and humans spot-checked them.
Actual operationalized methodology.anchor: Rather than coding student turns against a predefined code

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.anchor: categories are allowed to emerge from the data

Dataset name.value: Week-8 Socratic AI tutor logs from an introductory mechanics course
Dataset name.anchor: Our corpus of data comes from the Socratic AI tutor

Public or restricted data.value: restricted course interaction logs; public release not reported

Number of documents.value: 2,874 student turns within 5,513 total messages and 221 completed sessions

Approximate corpus size.value: 2,874 student messages; 833 raw labels consolidated to 357 categories

Prompting strategy.value: Emergent free-text labeling with the previous four student/tutor turns as context; context windows of 0, 2, 4, and 8 were piloted.
Prompting strategy.anchor: prompt provided the previous four conversational turns

Human role.value: A human expert independently labeled a stratified 10% sample; the first author audited clustering coherence; cluster names were spot-checked.

Unit of analysis.value: individual student turn with four preceding conversational turns as context
Unit of analysis.anchor: read each turn and produce its own short free

Generated outputs.value: 833 raw discourse labels, 357 consolidated categories, and two higher-level thematic bands

Evidence/provenance mechanism.value: Message-level logs, raw-to-consolidated category mapping, and expert-coded sampled turns
Evidence/provenance mechanism.anchor: Logging captured all turns at the message level

Baselines.value: Independent free-text labels from one human expert on 287 student messages

Number of runs or seeds.value: Context-window pilot (0, 2, 4, 8 turns) and clustering-threshold sweep from 0.20 to 0.60; no stochastic multi-seed evaluation reported

Automatic metrics.value: Cohen's kappa and raw agreement after mapping human and LLM labels to the consolidated taxonomy

Human-evaluation design.value: Independent expert labeling of a stratified 10% corpus sample plus a single-rater coherence audit of 50 groups

Number and expertise of evaluators.value: One human expert coder and one first-author clustering auditor; further expertise not reported

Principal results.value: The top 25 categories covered about 52% of student turns and categories with at least five messages covered 86%; equation handling and meta-procedural requests dominated the distribution.

Author-reported limitations.value: Authors report a single-site, single-course, single-tutor, mostly single-problem corpus; observational design; a 10% single-expert reliability sample; a single-rater clustering audit; and model-contingent category boundaries.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: substantial agreement with one expert and face-validity checks do not establish interpretive validity or transferability; the pooled taxonomy remains contingent on the selected model, embedding, and clustering threshold.
Additional validity concerns.anchor: single-rater coherence judgments establish only face validity

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Direct baseline for inductive dialogue coding, raw-to-theme provenance, threshold sensitivity, and expert-validation design.

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: arXiv methodological preprint; no peer-reviewed publication identified by 2026-08-24
records.decision_reason: The paper provides a directly applicable human-centered methodological workflow and reproducibility materials, but does not report a completed empirical evaluation of qualitative theme generation.

Research objective.value: Specify a human-centered API workflow for LLM-supported annotation, summarization, and information extraction in content analysis.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: Qualitative and quantitative content analysis with LLM-supported annotation, summarization, and extraction.
Claimed qualitative methodology.anchor: three qualitative and quantitative content analysis tasks

Actual operationalized methodology.value: A methodological workflow in which researchers define constructs and sampling, author a versioned promptbook, validate outputs, retain interpretive authority, and document provenance; it is not an empirical comparison study.
Actual operationalized methodology.anchor: Researchers specify constructs and sampling strategies

Model family.value: general large language models accessed through APIs

Human role.value: Researchers design, supervise, validate, and interpret every stage.
Human role.anchor: validate its outputs, and retain interpretive authority

Generated outputs.value: Annotations/codes, summaries, extracted information, validation reports, and audit documentation

Evidence/provenance mechanism.value: Versioned promptbook, saved model inputs/outputs, validation samples, and researcher decisions are prescribed as an audit trail.
Evidence/provenance mechanism.anchor: outputs are candidates for evidence that must be verified

Reproducibility resources.value: Supplementary prompt library, Python code, and Jupyter Notebook usage instructions

Author-reported limitations.value: Authors emphasize black-box behavior, prompt sensitivity, hallucination, data-governance risk, and the need for human validation.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: this is prescriptive methodological guidance rather than an independent empirical validation; effectiveness and feasibility therefore depend on future applications.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Contextual source for promptbooks, auditability, human authority, sampling, and validation requirements.

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: peer-reviewed journal article, British Journal of Psychiatry, published online/in issue by 2026-08-24
records.decision_reason: GPT-4o is used for structured parsing with human quality assurance; qualitative themes are developed manually, making the study adjacent evidence for extraction and verification rather than a core LLM thematic-analysis study.

Research objective.value: Describe the profile, relational patterns, concerns, and preventive actions in mental-health-related Prevention of Future Death reports.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: Network analysis and manual thematic analysis, with LLM-assisted structured parsing.

Actual operationalized methodology.value: Public reports were scraped and OCR-processed; GPT-4o parsed demographics and structured attributes under revised prompts; humans performed targeted quality assurance and manually developed the final themes through iterative review.

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: hybrid; structured extraction plus inductive manual thematic review

Domain.value: mental-health mortality and coronial prevention reports in England and Wales

Dataset name.value: Public Prevention of Future Death reports through June 2025

Human role.value: Humans refined prompts, quality-checked parsed fields, and conducted the final thematic analysis.

Generated outputs.value: Structured report attributes, networks, manually derived themes, and temporal patterns

Evidence/provenance mechanism.value: Public source reports, supplementary extraction prompts, and targeted manual validation

Baselines.value: Targeted manual validation of automated extraction; no LLM-versus-human theme-generation comparison

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: Public coronial records; research-ethics review and data-handling discussion reported

Author-reported limitations.value: Authors report incomplete/uneven report availability, possible missing PFDRs, and limitations inherent in the observational public-record corpus.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: the LLM's contribution is parsing, not interpretive theme development; extraction accuracy cannot establish validity of the human thematic conclusions.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Adjacent example of a defensible division of labor: LLM extraction with human verification and human-led interpretation.

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: peer-reviewed open-access journal article in Scientific Reports, published 2026
records.decision_reason: The study uses GPT models for sentiment filtering and theory-driven multi-label qualitative coding, validates a sample against a human, and integrates codes into a QFD framework.

Research objective.value: Adapt Quality Function Deployment to translate patient feedback into prioritized technical requirements for human-centered healthcare AI.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: LLM-driven thematic coding within a five-phase Quality Function Deployment workflow.

Actual operationalized methodology.value: A fraud classifier filtered reviews; GPT-4o-mini identified negative reviews; GPT-4 assigned 41 predefined multi-label categories refined in three pilots; a human sample was validated; factor analysis and a three-expert Delphi informed the QFD matrix.

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: deductive coding with iterative codebook refinement

Domain.value: patient experience in Malaysian private hospitals and healthcare-AI design

Dataset name.value: Google Maps reviews of 53 private hospitals in Selangor, Malaysia

Number of documents.value: 14,938 reviews collected; 12,035 with text; 1,279 negative reviews coded

Approximate corpus size.value: 1,279 coded negative reviews after screening 14,938 reviews

Exact model/version.value: GPT-4o mini and GPT-4; API snapshots not reported

Prompting strategy.value: Structured prompt containing 41 literature-derived categories; multi-label assignment; three 100-review pilot rounds with expert feedback

Human role.value: Experts refined prompts, validated 200 reviews, and a three-member domain panel performed a modified Delphi for technical requirements.
Human role.anchor: Human validation on a random sample of 200

Generated outputs.value: 41 thematic codes, six latent constructs, ten patient-quality dimensions, and a House of Quality priority matrix

Baselines.value: Human coding on a random 200-review sample and expert consensus for QFD mappings

Automatic metrics.value: Fraud-classifier precision/recall/accuracy; Cohen's kappa; KMO/Bartlett tests; Cronbach alpha; factor and sensitivity analyses

Human-evaluation design.value: Human validation of 200 randomly sampled reviews plus modified Delphi consensus among three domain experts

Number and expertise of evaluators.value: One or more human review validators not fully enumerated; Delphi panel of three (QFD/quality specialist, physician, psychometric/statistical expert)

Statistical analysis.value: Exploratory factor analysis with Varimax rotation, KMO/Bartlett tests, Cronbach alpha, correlations, QFD weighting, and sensitivity analysis

Principal results.value: Coding yielded 41 codes consolidated into ten dimensions; kappa was 0.81; granular categorization received the highest technical-priority score, but projected improvements were not deployment outcomes.

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: Public reviews; no personally identifiable information stored; IRB not required under cited Malaysian guidance; platform terms followed.

Reproducibility resources.value: Supplementary code lists and factor-analysis tables; executable code and exact model snapshots not reported

Author-reported limitations.value: Authors report one national/private-hospital setting, expert-panel sampling, a fallible fraud filter, negative-review restriction, public-data consent concerns, theoretical rather than deployed improvement estimates, and no real-world outcome test.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: predefined categories and frequency/QFD weighting support descriptive prioritization, not inductive interpretive discovery; kappa on one sample does not validate the QFD causal or implementation claims.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Useful comparator for deductive multi-label coding, human-AI reliability, expert-panel validation, and the risk of converting code frequency into design priorities.

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: peer-reviewed open-access PLOS ONE article, published 2026
records.decision_reason: The paper performs LLM-assisted inductive thematic synthesis of a defined outcome-domain corpus followed by iterative expert refinement and consensus.

Research objective.value: Create a provisional descriptive framework that organizes outcome domains from existing neurological Core Outcome Sets.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: Modified five-step inductive thematic analysis/framework synthesis without predetermined codes.

Actual operationalized methodology.value: COMET outcome domains were longlisted; ChatGPT 3.5, Gemini 1.5 Flash, and Llama-2-70B were tested through six prompt refinements; clinicians selected ChatGPT output, reduced/organized domains, and used a three-round modified nominal-group consensus with OMERACT as a scaffold.

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: hybrid: initially inductive LLM grouping, then expert/OMERACT-guided hierarchical refinement
Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.anchor: themes were created without any predetermined codes

Dataset name.value: COMET neurological Core Outcome Set records fixed at August 2022
Dataset name.anchor: analytic dataset was fixed at August 2022

Public or restricted data.value: public/published COS records in the COMET database

Approximate corpus size.value: 782 extracted outcome entries reduced to 218 domains before final expert synthesis

Model family.value: OpenAI ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Meta Llama

Exact model/version.value: ChatGPT 3.5, Gemini 1.5 Flash, Llama-2-70B; provider snapshots not reported

Prompting strategy.value: Six iterative prompts; final prompt requested inductive analysis using the OMERACT concept/core-area/domain hierarchy as an example

Single-agent or multi-agent.value: three-model comparison followed by single-model-assisted expert synthesis
Single-agent or multi-agent.anchor: Outputs from ChatGPT, Gemini and Meta

Human role.value: Six purposively selected clinicians/researchers reviewed outputs, resolved discrepancies, revised categories, and retained conceptual authority.

Generated outputs.value: A framework of four concepts, 13 core areas, and 75 domains

Evidence/provenance mechanism.value: COMET IDs, longlists, supplemental prompt/output files, recorded expert revisions, and domain-to-framework tables
Evidence/provenance mechanism.anchor: coded based on the COMET ID

Baselines.value: Cross-model comparison and expert review; no formal human-only thematic-analysis baseline
Baselines.anchor: formal benchmarking against human-only analysis was not conducted

Number of runs or seeds.value: Six prompt iterations and qualitative session-consistency checks; no formal stochastic reruns

Human-evaluation design.value: Three-round modified nominal-group process with independent written review, a consensus meeting, and final approval

Number and expertise of evaluators.value: Six neurologists, neurosurgeons, and clinical/outcomes researchers from the UK, Switzerland, and United States

Inter-rater reliability.value: Consensus threshold at least 75%; formal inter-rater coefficient not reported

Principal results.value: ChatGPT was selected over Gemini and Llama; experts transformed 782 entries into a provisional framework of four concepts, 13 core areas, and 75 domains.

Efficiency or cost results.value: Authors state preliminary organization appeared faster, but did not quantify efficiency.

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: Analysis used published COS records; participant-level sensitive data were not analyzed; further ethics reporting not material

Reproducibility resources.value: Supplementary longlist, prompts, and ChatGPT output are reported; executable code and exact service snapshots are not reported

Author-reported limitations.value: Authors call the framework provisional and hypothesis-generating, note the small expert group and absence of formal multi-stakeholder consensus, no human-only benchmark, prompt/model sensitivity, and no quantified efficiency.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: using OMERACT in the final prompt and expert restructuring makes the final framework hybrid rather than purely inductive; consensus among six experts is not evidence of patient/stakeholder validity.
Additional validity concerns.anchor: does not constitute a formal multi-stakeholder consensus

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Strong example of cross-model screening, expert authority, hierarchical provenance, and explicit limits on autonomous thematic synthesis.

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: peer-reviewed open-access journal article in Healthcare, published 2026
records.decision_reason: The study applies several LLM platforms and latent semantic analysis to leadership interviews and compares resulting themes, while retaining important comparator and validity limitations.

Research objective.value: Test whether accessible AI tools can analyze interviews with chief nursing officers and identify organizational-quality factors missed by prior manual analysis.
Research objective.anchor: Interview data from chief nursing officers

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: AI-enhanced qualitative/content analysis compared with latent semantic analysis and prior human interpretation.

Actual operationalized methodology.value: Leadership interview transcripts were analyzed with traditional latent semantic analysis and queried through Gemini 2.5; the authors also reviewed Scholar AI 5.1, Copilot Chat, and Claude Sonnet 4.5 outputs and mapped identified factors to the Donabedian framework.

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: hybrid exploratory theme identification and theory mapping

Dataset name.value: Semistructured chief nursing officer interviews from top-performing academic medical centers

Model family.value: Google Gemini, ScholarAI, Microsoft Copilot, Anthropic Claude

Exact model/version.value: Gemini 2.5; Scholar AI 5.1; Copilot Chat; Claude Sonnet 4.5

Human role.value: Researchers selected data and prompts, compared outputs with latent-semantic/manual findings, and interpreted theoretical linkages.

Generated outputs.value: Ten primary factors and 24 subtopics plus a proposed linkage to Donabedian's structure-process-outcomes model

Baselines.value: Traditional latent semantic analysis and a prior manual analysis of the interviews

Human-evaluation design.value: Researcher comparison and interpretation; independent blinded qualitative evaluation not reported

Principal results.value: LLM analysis produced ten factors/24 subtopics and surfaced a Donabedian linkage the authors state manual analysis had missed; analysis time was described as near-instantaneous versus weeks.

Efficiency or cost results.value: Authors report weeks for traditional analysis versus nearly instantaneous LLM output; formal time/cost protocol not reported

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: University IRB approval and written informed consent were reported.

Reproducibility resources.value: Supplementary tables provide illustrative themes; prompts/code and exact provider snapshots were not fully reported

Author-reported limitations.value: Authors acknowledge small/selective leadership data, model and prompt dependence, and limits to generalizing the proposed organizational framework.
Author-reported limitations.anchor: This work is not without limitations

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: the paper does not report a blinded independent human evaluation or a common scoring protocol across platforms; a theoretically plausible missed linkage is not proof of deeper interpretive validity.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Comparator for cross-tool qualitative analysis, efficiency claims, and the distinction between novelty of output and validated interpretation.
